er_v06_c18_b101_01: The next afternoon, two people come to the window, one behind the other. The first carries half a sack of secondhand goods.
er_v06_c18_b101_02: We agreed I'd be the one to bring her! Then she starts running over here by herself every day — what does that make me?
er_v06_c18_b101_03: It makes you the guide. I knew the way already.
er_v06_c18_b101_05: Just tell me—hasn't she been looking better lately? Face is a little rounder.
er_v06_c18_b101_06: Whose face is round. Cut it out.
er_v06_c18_b101_07: Lydia lifts her wrist and gives it a shake. The old bracelet glints under the light.
er_v06_c18_b101_08: I wear the bracelet every day. When my family asks, I say I found it myself.
er_v06_c18_b101_09: Oh, enough about the bracelet. I'm here to see her today.
er_v06_c18_b101_10: My family's been going through my accounts lately. I have to be back before dinner. I got her here.
er_v06_c18_b101_11: Next time I'll come on my own. I've got things to buy too. That's settled, then.
er_v06_c18_b101_13: One bracelet's worth of friendship. I'm off!
er_v06_c18_b101_14: Eleanor sets the sack on the counter. Metal parts clink inside; she takes her time untying it.
er_v06_c18_b101_15: She talks a lot. Don't take it all seriously.
er_v06_c18_b101_16: The room's registered now. Mother sleeps in the bed at the back.
er_v06_c18_b101_17: She came here yesterday. After she got back, she didn't say a word to me.
er_v06_c18_b101_18: She bought household goods, and something to eat.
er_v06_c18_b101_20: That's all. Paid the marked price.
er_v06_c18_b101_22: She opens the sack and tips out an old box, its lid split along a seam. And a roll of coiled wire.
er_v06_c18_b101_23: The crack's in the lid. The bottom's fine. I measured the wire myself. Nothing broken.
er_v06_c18_b101_25: Box goes as secondhand. Wire counts as a full roll.
er_v06_c18_b101_26: About what I figured. A little less and I'd still take it.
er_v06_c18_b101_27: She puts the coins in her purse, ties it twice, and stays at the window.
